subject: NovaApps prepay structure + true-up reconciliation options
messages:
From: Sara Koh <sara@novaapps.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@novaapps.com
Date: 2026-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Prepay structure + true-up question

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's performance profile. Before we get legal and procurement involved, we need to understand how prepay true-up works in practice for a multi-year commitment. We are considering a 3-year prepay with a ramp: Year 1 = 50% of expected usage, Year 2 = 75%, Year 3 = 100%. Our questions: 

- How do you handle end-of-term reconciliation? Do you typically invoice overage at list or at a discounted rate?
- What buffer band would you recommend to avoid surprise overage bills? We were suggested a 10% band internally but want to know what's standard for Redwood.
- Do unused prepay credits rollover between years or expire at the term boundary?

We also need to understand whether a monthly smoothing/true-up is possible (so we don't get a big invoice at EOT), and what the impact on pricing is if we want a firm cap on overage charges.

Can you share an example of a reconciliation calculation and any sample language you include in the term sheet? Procurement will want to see a clear clause for netting/credits.

Best,
Sara Koh
VP Product Operations
NovaApps
procurement@novaapps.com


From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Koh <sara@novaapps.com>

Subject: Re: Prepay structure + true-up question

Sara — great to hear and thanks for the clear questions. High level answers below and I attached a starter term sheet + a redline of the true-up clause so you can see wording.

Short answers:
- End-of-term reconciliation: two common patterns we support — (A) EOT true-up where actual usage above the prepay is invoiced at the committed discount (or list if no discount), or (B) Monthly smoothing where overages are billed month-to-month and credited against remaining prepay. EOT true-up is more common for multi-year prepay contracts.
- Buffer band: we typically see 5–15% bands. For your ramp profile a 7–10% buffer is reasonable; larger buffers increase cost but reduce billing surprises.
- Rollover: default is no indefinite carry-forward — unused prepay typically reconciles at EOT. We can offer limited rollover (90-day) by exception for multi-year deals.

Example calculation (simple):
- Committed prepay (annually): 1,000,000 tokens at $0.01/token (effective discounted rate)
- Actual usage year: 1,080,000 tokens
- Buffer band: 7% => threshold = 1,070,000 tokens (1,000,000 * 1.07)
- Billed overage at EOT = 10,000 tokens billed at agreed overage rate (often list price or list minus a smaller discount)

Options for NovaApps:
- Conservative: 7% buffer, EOT true-up, overage billed at list - 10% (cap), no rollover.
- Smoothing: monthly overage billing up to remaining prepay, with EOT reconciliation and smaller end-of-term invoice.

I've attached: NovaApps_term_sheet_v1.pdf (starter numbers) and redline_trueup_clause.docx. Happy to walk procurement through examples on a quick call.

Cheers,

Folks — forwarding Sara's note and my reply. Procurement is asking for clarity on buffer and reconciliation. Draft proposal ideas below; need pricing + legal guidance before I respond with a firm term sheet.

Proposed commercial structure (your quick read):
- 3-year prepay, annual invoices by year.
- Pricing: tiered committed discount by year-on-year ramp; suggested list: Year1 = 20% off list (for 50% commit), Year2 = 25% off, Year3 = 30% off once at 100% commit.
- Buffer: 7% by default; overage billed at list price minus the committed discount for that year (cap overage to at most 1.25x list if finance needs protection).
- Reconciliation: 60-day EOT true-up window, invoice/credit netting. No indefinite carry-forward; allow a 90-day one-time rollover for deployment delays.

Key asks for pricing/legal:
1) Approve Year1 20% or suggest alternative?
2) Finance: OK to bill overage at list - committed discount? Do we need a cap?
3) Legal: wording for smoothing vs EOT true-up — which do we default to for this deal?

I can present either conservative or customer-friendly option. Recommend we go slightly conservative on Year1 pricing given usage uncertainty; we can include a performance credit if they ramp faster.

Thanks — B

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: NovaApps prepay structure + true-up question — pricing ask

Ben — thanks for the summary. A few quick notes from finance/product: 

- Pricing: drop Year1 to 15% off list; offer an accelerator credit in Year3 (e.g., additional one-time credit if they hit >110% usage vs committed). This protects margin while keeping upside.
- Overage billing: finance prefers EOT invoice at list minus committed discount. Please add a hard cap clause (we usually recommend a 1.2x list cap for one-off overshoots).
- Reconciliation window: 60 days is fine. Legal will want to see explicit language about claims after reconciliation period being waived.
- Rollover: allow 90-day rollover only for force-majeure or deployment delays, else no carry-forward.

If you send me the updated term sheet (with the above), we can route to legal and pricing for signoff.

Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks for the patience. Based on internal guidance I've attached an updated term sheet (NovaApps_term_sheet_v2.pdf) and included the redlined true-up language. Summary of the proposal below: 

- Structure: 3-year prepay with annual commitments (Year1 50%, Year2 75%, Year3 100%).
- Pricing: Year1 = 15% off list, Year2 = 22% off, Year3 = 30% off. One-time Year3 accelerator credit if usage >110% of committed in year 3.
- Buffer band: 7% by default.
- Overage: EOT true-up; overage billed at list price minus that year's committed discount, capped at 1.2x list for isolated overshoots.
- Reconciliation: 60-day EOT window. After 60 days the reconciliation amount is final and claims are waived.
- Rollover: one-time 90-day rollover for documented deployment delays; otherwise unused prepay is reconciled at EOT.

Attachments: NovaApps_term_sheet_v2.pdf (updated numbers), redline_trueup_clause.docx (final wording). If this aligns, I'll open a DocuSign draft for MSA + SOW and we can route through procurement.
